How this works
Groups of 4–5, with three roles:
SPEAKER
Presents your group's thinking to the room
SKEPTIC
Must find what could go wrong. Disagreeing is your job
SCRIBE
Writes your ideas down, big enough to hold up
Ground rules: no right answers, only good reasons. "It depends" is allowed, if you say on what. Rotate roles every part.

PART 1 · ABOUT 6 MINUTES
Blockchain or not?
  • Six everyday situations, one gut call each
  • One hand up = BLOCKCHAIN · two hands = DATABASE · arms crossed = IT DEPENDS
  • Then someone defends their vote in one sentence
PART 1 OF 4
PART 1 · BLOCKCHAIN OR NOT? · 1 OF 2
One hand up = BLOCKCHAIN · two hands = DATABASE · arms crossed = IT DEPENDS
Your college's attendance register
Your vote?
DATABASE
One trusted keeper, the college, writes it. Nobody needs strangers to agree on it. A spreadsheet wins.
Who owns which plot of land
Your vote?
IT DEPENDS
A tamper-evident history helps fight later forgery, but if an official enters a false record, the chain keeps the lie forever.
Sending money to a stranger in another country
Your vote?
BLOCKCHAIN
Two parties, no shared bank, neither trusts the other. This is the original use case for Bitcoin and stablecoins.
PART 1 · BLOCKCHAIN OR NOT?
PART 1 · BLOCKCHAIN OR NOT? · 2 OF 2
One hand up = BLOCKCHAIN · two hands = DATABASE · arms crossed = IT DEPENDS
Your full medical history
Your vote?
DATABASE
Never put personal data on a public chain: it can never be deleted. At most, store proofs or permissions there.
Items you own inside an online game
Your vote?
IT DEPENDS
If you want to keep and trade them even if the game company shuts down, yes. If not, the company's database is simpler.
The likes on your Instagram post
Your vote?
DATABASE
Nobody needs a global, tamper-proof record of likes. Some problems just aren't that serious.
PART 1 · BLOCKCHAIN OR NOT?
YOUR TOOL FOR THE REST OF THE SESSION
Four questions before you reach for a blockchain
1
Do several parties need to write to the same record?
2
Do they distrust each other, and any single middleman?
3
Must the record be tamper-evident and always available?
4
Can the data be public, or proven without revealing it?
Any "no"? A normal database, a better law or a better process is probably the answer.

Case files
  • Real problems that really happened

  • Then we look at what researchers and builders have tried
PART 2 OF 4
CASE FILE 01 · EXAM PAPER LEAKS
Who should guard the question paper?
In 2024, India's NEET-UG medical entrance exam, taken by more than 20 lakh students, was hit by paper-leak allegations. The CBI investigated and the case reached the Supreme Court.
Before any exam, a paper passes through many hands: setters, printers, transporters, strongrooms, exam centres. One dishonest link is enough to ruin it for everyone.
DISCUSS · 3 MINUTES
1
Where on its journey can a paper leak, and who do we have to trust at each step?
2
Could cryptography remove the need to trust any single person? How?
3
Skeptic: what would still go wrong, even with your fix?
PART 2 · CASE FILE 01
Widely reported, June–July 2024
CASE FILE 01 · WHAT PEOPLE HAVE TRIED
Decentralize the trust, not the paper
IDEAS WORTH STEALING
  • Encrypt every paper and split the unlock key among several independent officials, so no single person can open it early
  • Release the key only minutes before the exam
  • Record every access on a tamper-evident log anyone can audit
WHAT NO BLOCKCHAIN FIXES
  • Someone photographing the paper before it is encrypted
  • A corrupt exam centre or invigilator
  • A log is only as honest as whoever writes to it
Cryptography can remove single points of trust. It can't remove people from the physical world.
PART 2 · CASE FILE 01
CASE FILE 02 · FAKE MEDICINES
Is this medicine real?
In 2022 the WHO linked the deaths of dozens of children in The Gambia to contaminated cough syrups made by an Indian manufacturer.
The WHO estimates that about 1 in 10 medical products in low- and middle-income countries is substandard or falsified. Since August 2023, India has required QR codes on the packs of its 300 top-selling drug brands.
DISCUSS · 3 MINUTES
1
Where can a fake or bad batch enter the chain from factory to patient?
2
Who should keep the record of where each box has been: the company, the government, or everyone?
3
Skeptic: if every box has a code on a blockchain, what can a fraudster still do?
PART 2 · CASE FILE 02
WHO medical product alerts (2022) · WHO (2017) · CDSCO (2023)
CASE FILE 02 · WHAT PEOPLE HAVE TRIED
A chain records claims, not chemistry
IDEAS WORTH STEALING
  • Register each box at the factory and record every hand-off, signed by whoever handled it
  • Let independent labs publish signed test results, so the maker isn't the only voice
  • Let any patient scan a pack and see its full journey
WHAT NO BLOCKCHAIN FIXES
  • A bad batch registered as "good" stays "good" forever
  • Codes can be copied onto fake boxes
  • Someone still has to test what's inside
Decentralize the checking, not just the record-keeping.
PART 2 · CASE FILE 02
CASE FILE 03 · WHO HOLDS YOUR MONEY?
The exchange that vanished in a week
In November 2022, FTX, one of the world's biggest crypto exchanges, collapsed within days. Customers learned their deposits had been secretly used elsewhere; about $8 billion was missing.
Its founder was convicted of fraud and sentenced to 25 years in prison. Millions of customers had trusted a company to hold their coins, like a bank, but without a bank's rules.
DISCUSS · 3 MINUTES
1
Who really controlled the customers' money, and who could check?
2
How could customers have found out before it was too late?
3
Skeptic: if everyone holds their own keys instead, what new risks appear?
PART 2 · CASE FILE 03
US court records and reporting, 2022–2024
CASE FILE 03 · WHAT PEOPLE HAVE TRIED
Your keys, your coins, your problem
IDEAS WORTH STEALING
  • Proof of reserves: exchanges publish cryptographic proof that they hold what they owe, which each user can check
  • Self-custody: hold your own keys, so nobody can lend out your money
  • Exchanges built as smart contracts, where every trade settles in public
WHAT NO BLOCKCHAIN FIXES
  • Lose your seed phrase or get phished, and nobody can help you
  • A one-day snapshot of reserves can be faked with borrowed money
  • Most people don't want to be their own bank
Making self-custody safe for ordinary people is still an open problem.
PART 2 · CASE FILE 03
CASE FILE 04 · DEEPFAKES
Is this video real?
During India's 2024 general election, AI-generated videos of politicians spread widely, including speeches by leaders who had died years earlier.
Making a convincing fake now costs almost nothing. Checking one costs a lot, and by the time it's checked, millions have seen it.
DISCUSS · 3 MINUTES
1
How could anyone prove that a video is genuine?
2
Who should decide what gets labelled fake: platforms, the government, or everyone?
3
Skeptic: what goes wrong with each of those choices?
PART 2 · CASE FILE 04
Widely reported, April–June 2024
CASE FILE 04 · WHAT PEOPLE HAVE TRIED
Prove the source, not the truth
IDEAS WORTH STEALING
  • Content credentials: cameras and apps sign a file's origin and every edit, so anyone can check it
  • Proof of personhood, so accounts belong to real, unique people
  • Public, tamper-evident registries of signed originals
WHAT NO BLOCKCHAIN FIXES
  • Billions of old, unsigned videos
  • A fake can be re-filmed off a screen
  • "Who decides what's true" is a social question; decentralization spreads that power, it doesn't answer it
Cryptography can prove who made something. Only people can judge whether it's true.
PART 2 · CASE FILE 04
PART 3 · ABOUT 6 MINUTES
The great debate
  • One motion, two sides
  • FOR team: 60 seconds · AGAINST team: 60 seconds · rebuttals: 30 seconds each
  • The room votes before and after: did anyone change their mind?
PART 3 OF 4
THE MOTION
"This house believes UPI would be better on a public blockchain."
NEED A NUDGE? FOR COULD SAY…
  • No single operator that can go down, freeze or block you
  • Anyone in the world could build payment apps on it
  • Money that can follow rules automatically
NEED A NUDGE? AGAINST COULD SAY…
  • UPI already handles billions of payments a month, fast and free
  • On a public chain, anyone could see your payments
  • Fraud and mistakes couldn't be reversed. Who protects users?
PART 3 · THE GREAT DEBATE

Design sprint

  • Your Skeptic attacks your design before you present it

PART 4 · DESIGN SPRINT · 5 MINUTES
Design a student election nobody can rig
01
Only enrolled students can vote
02
One student, one vote
03
Nobody can see how you voted
04
Anyone can verify the final count
05
Works on a phone, in a single day
ON YOUR PAPER
Three boxes: who can vote, how votes are counted, how anyone checks the count.
Then your Skeptic has one minute to break it. Fix what they find.
PART 4 · DESIGN SPRINT
PART 4 · HOW RESEARCHERS APPROACH IT
Prove you can vote, not who you are
01 · ELIGIBILITY
The college issues every student a digital credential, once.
02 · ANONYMITY
Vote with a zero-knowledge proof: "I'm an eligible student who hasn't voted yet", and nothing more.
03 · A COUNT ANYONE CAN CHECK
Encrypted votes are posted publicly, so anyone can recount.
04 · STILL UNSOLVED
Vote-buying: if you can prove how you voted, someone can pay you for it.

TAKE THESE WITH YOU
Three questions for any system you meet
Who has the power here?
How could it be abused?
What makes abuse impossible, or visible?
Sometimes the answer is a blockchain. Often it's a better database, a better law or a better process. Knowing the difference is the skill. See you on the road to Mumbai.
